judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare insuring recital conditioning coverage on payment of premium and 'ALL THE TERMS OF THIS POLICY'; the only defect is the OCR-level typo 'THES POLICY', which does not change meaning. Nothing here names a term a court would have to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a general subject-to clause that harmonises with the Coverage Part declarations and the Commercial Property Conditions rather than conflicting with them. I found no operative provision it contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely administrative statement of which coverage parts are included, with 'may be subject to adjustment' left open but not operative. No named ambiguity of consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Calculation of Premium Endorsement and Premium Audit condition, which supply the adjustment mechanism. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'INSURANCE AT THE DESCRIBED PREMISES APPLIES ONLY FOR THE COVERAGES SHOWN BELOW' is a limiting formula whose reach against blanket limits could be argued, but the phrase itself is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations list blanket building/contents/business income limits across nine premises, so the 'described premises' limitation sits somewhat awkwardly with C. Limits Of Insurance and the blanket-limit computation in A.4.e. Some tension, but harmonisable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line schedule note; 'subject to the General Aggregate Limit' is definite. No lexical uncertainty to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Definition V.16.b.(3) removes from the 'products-completed operations hazard' any operations whose classification says they are subject to the General Aggregate Limit, yet the Declarations still show a separate Products-Completed Operations Aggregate Limit of $2,000,000. That is a real, if minor, internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard first-named-insured cancellation right; 'advance written notice' is undefined as to length but the insured controls it. Very little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits beside A.2 and the Kansas Changes endorsement IL 02 61, which replaces only paragraph 2 and leaves paragraph 1 intact. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise 10-day/30-day notice mechanics; the only flaws are OCR misspellings. Nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 02 61 (Kansas Changes) expressly replaces this very paragraph with a longer version adding statutory grounds, so the printed text is superseded and duplicated at c073. Express replacement mostly cures it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'last mailing address known to us' is a familiar and workable standard. No naming-worthy ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors IL 02 61 B.2's nonrenewal notice provision without contradicting it. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Simple and definite: notice states the date, the policy period ends then. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Installment Payments condition and the Kansas cancellation endorsement. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the refund may be less than pro rata' leaves the short-rate amount unstated, a small but real openness. Otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Premiums condition making the first Named Insured payee of return premiums. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence evidentiary rule that is definite on its face. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated verbatim in IL 02 61 B.2 for nonrenewal; consistent. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration plus no-oral-modification clause; 'all the agreements between you and us' is broad but standard. Modest risk from the interplay of 'authorized to make changes ... with our consent' and 'only by endorsement'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with numerous endorsements that expressly amend terms, which is the mechanism it prescribes. No contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Audit right limited in time and subject matter; definite. Only OCR corruption of words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements Duties In The Event Of Loss (E.3.a.(6)) and CGL Premium Audit. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This printing says 'We have the right to' and then separately disclaims obligation, and it cross-refers to 'Paragraphs 1. and 2. of this condition' when its own subparagraphs are lettered a., b., c. — a cross-reference that does not land. 'warrent' and the dangling cross-reference are mechanical errors affecting meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cover-jacket duplicate at c080 reads 'We have the right but are not obligated to' and numbers the subparagraphs 1.-3., so the two printings of the same condition differ. That inconsistency is a genuine whole-instrument problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, definite obligations. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Installment Payments and Premium Audit provisions. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Anti-assignment language; 'rights and duties ... may not be transferred without our written consent' is often argued as to post-loss assignments, though the words themselves are plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses assignment; the mortgageholder condition operates independently. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'we will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deemed-election formula, and the notice must 'specify the date and time of cancelation'. Slightly loose but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second printing of the same condition (c083) requires the notice to specify only 'the date of cancellation', so the two versions in one instrument differ. Also sits against Kansas cancellation grounds in IL 02 61.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An applicability lead-in, garbled by OCR but substantively a pointer. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated at c084 in fuller form; the two are compatible. No real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'void in any case of fraud' plus 'intentionally conceal or misrepresent a material fact' — 'material' is a stock but genuinely contestable standard. Moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (Kansas Changes) replaces this condition entirely with a narrower 'we will not pay' formulation, so the printed voidness language conflicts with the controlling endorsement. Express replacement largely resolves it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'beyond your direction or control' is a workable standard; the breach-of-condition sentence is location-specific and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 supersedes this condition, but only 'when coverage is provided for townhouse buildings', which this apartment risk is not. Latent but unlikely tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short anti-stacking rule; 'the actual amount of the loss or damage' is definite enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on whether Building, Contents and Business Income blanket coverages can overlap, and sits against Limits Of Insurance and the additional-insurance statements in the Coverage Extensions. Some tension but no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-year suit limitation tied to the date 'the direct physical loss or damage occurred'; the trigger date is clear, though 'full compliance with all of the terms' is a broad condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A. (Kansas Changes) replaces this very condition with a five-year period, and the same two-year text is reprinted at c088 — so the instrument contains both limits. That is a direct conflict, mitigated only by the express replacement language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Liberalization clause with a defined 45-day window; definite. Nothing to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Changes condition requiring endorsement, since this is an automatic-broadening exception. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly OCR-corrupted ('YO BENEFIT TO BAILEE', 'cusdy'), but the substance is the familiar one-line bailee rule. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reprinted intact at c090 and consistent with the Personal Property Of Others provisions. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pro-rata and excess other-insurance mechanics stated with arithmetic precision. Little room to argue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated at c091 in the same terms and consistent with the excess wording in the Non-Owned Trailers extension. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'loss or damage commencing' during the policy period and within a listed territory; definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Period of Restoration definition's statement that policy expiration will not cut short the period. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subrogation transfer plus an enumerated list of parties whose rights may be waived after loss ('Your tenant' etc.) — an expressio unius list, but a closed and clear one. This printing says 'to or for whom'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The second printing of the identical condition (c094) says 'to or from whom', a discrepancy between two versions of one condition; CP 01 01 E. also supersedes it for Builders' Risk. Minor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long nuclear-energy exclusion drafted with heavy defined-term scaffolding; dense but internally precise. Little to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It modifies CGL/Liquor/Auto parts, and Liquor and Auto coverage parts are not in this policy — a surplus rather than a conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definitions are severely mangled in this printing ('Hazardous properties include radioacti\ explosive propertles', a definition of 'Source material' with no predicate), so several defined terms have no usable content. That is a mechanical failure that changes meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines terms used only in the nuclear endorsement; no other provision depends on them. Little relational risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward renewal-rating provision. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reprinted at c092 and consistent with Premium Audit. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Entitlement to a dividend 'if declared' is contingent but plainly so. Nothing to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These are 'CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO STATE AUTOMOBILE MUTUAL INSURANCE COMPANY', yet the Declarations name State Auto Property and Casualty Insurance Company as the issuing insurer — a membership/dividend right against a company that is not the insurer. Genuine, if rarely litigated, incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixes a place and time of meeting with precision. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Grants membership and voting rights in the mutual company while the Declarations identify a different, stock, insurer as the one providing this insurance. Same mismatch as the other mutual-company conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Non-assessability stated flatly; 'shall not be liable ... for any premium other than that stated in this policy' is definite. Very little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says no premium beyond that stated is owed, while the Premium Audit condition and the Calculation of Premium Endorsement contemplate additional earned premium — and it is headed as a mutual-company condition though the insurer is a stock company. That is a genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading instruction and pronoun key; definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Points to Section H. Definitions, which exists in the same form. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on 'direct physical loss of or damage to' Covered Property — the single most argued phrase in property insurance, though undefined here by design. Real but generic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by the Causes of Loss form, Limits, Deductible and Valuation, all of which fit it. No specific contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated definition of Building and Business Personal Property with '(4) All other personal property owned by you and used in your business' as a catch-all after specifics — mild ejusdem generis exposure. Otherwise itemised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with Property Not Covered and the Coverage Extensions; CP 01 01 C.3 adds an item only for townhouse risks. No conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long exclusion list with several broad members ('Land (including land on which the property is located)', property 'more specifically described' elsewhere); scope questions are conceivable but each item is enumerated. Moderate-low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.3 purports to add a paragraph 'q.' to Property Not Covered, but this printing already has a paragraph q. (outdoor property) — a lettering collision. Small but real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations do show 'SPECIAL FORM' and CP 10 30 is attached, so the reference lands. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Debris removal caps stated with worked arithmetic examples; the mechanics are unusually explicit. 'debris of Covered Property' is a possible boundary but a narrow one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with Limits Of Insurance (which does not list debris removal as additional) and with the Outdoor Property extension that includes debris removal expense. Minor tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow, time-limited preservation coverage; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly cross-referenced in C. Limits Of Insurance as not increasing the limit. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A $1,000 cap for two enumerated sources of fire-service liability; closed list, definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: C. Limits Of Insurance confirms this limit is in addition to the Limits. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pollutant clean-up limited to extraction from land or water with a $10,000 annual cap; 'pollutants' is defined. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Debris Removal carve-out for pollutant extraction and with the CP 10 30 pollution exclusion. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The blanket-limit sub-cap — 'the lesser of: $10,000 or 5% times the value of the damaged building as of the time of loss times the applicable coinsurance percentage' — is a formula that two sides can read very differently, and 'increased costs incurred to comply with enforcement of an ordinance or law' is itself a contested boundary. e.(8) even concedes that the Ordinance or Law Exclusion may 'conflict with' this coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the Ordinance Or Law Exclusion (B.1.a of CP 10 30), with Loss Payment E.4.b, with Valuation E.7.b and with the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage G.3.f, all of which say ordinance-driven costs are excluded. That web of carve-outs and counter-carve-outs is exactly the kind of whole-instrument problem a court has to sort out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Electronic data coverage with a stated $2,500 annual aggregate and detailed causation rules. Little to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coordinates with Property Not Covered n. and with the Business Income Interruption Of Computer Operations coverage. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional gateway ('If a Coinsurance percentage of 80% or more ... is shown'); definite and satisfied here at 100%. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Declarations' 100% coinsurance and with the Coinsurance Additional Condition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Newly acquired property extension with fixed dollar caps and a 30-day cut-off; enumerated and definite. 'Similar use as the building described in the Declarations' is a slight softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with the additional-insurance statement at the end of the Extensions and with Limits Of Insurance. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed $2,500 sub-limit and a theft carve-out; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Personal Property Of Others in A.1.c and the account-of-owner rule. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Valuable papers extension with an express $2,500 cap and a clear electronic-data carve-out. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Dovetails with Property Not Covered o. and the Electronic Data Additional Coverage. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Temporarily at a location you do not own, lease or operate' uses an undefined 'temporarily', a small but genuine vagueness. Otherwise capped and enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the 100-foot premises rule and the Property In Transit extension in CP 10 30. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Named-peril outdoor property extension with $1,000/$250 caps; a closed list. Little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 D. revises the $250 to $500 for Kansas, so the printed figure is superseded — an express, tidy amendment rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trailer extension with three cumulative conditions, two exclusions and a $5,000 cap; unusually tight. Nothing to name.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its excess-insurance sentence matches the Other Insurance condition. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Each of these Extensions is additional insurance unless otherwise indicated' — the 'unless otherwise indicated' hook requires hunting through each extension, a modest scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against the Valuable Papers extension, which says part of its payment is expressly not additional insurance, and against Limits Of Insurance which lists only some coverages as additional. Mild tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure cross-reference to the Causes of Loss form. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 10 30 is attached and supplies both exclusions and limitations. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The most we will pay for loss or damage in any one occurrence is the applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations' — 'applicable Limit' is doing heavy work where the Declarations show blanket limits over nine buildings. That is a nameable openness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the blanket-limit sub-cap in the Increased Cost Of Construction coverage, with the Coinsurance condition and with the additional-insurance statements in the Extensions. There is real tension over what the 'applicable Limit' is for a single damaged building under a blanket.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deductible sequencing spelled out step by step with two worked examples. Very little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly keyed to the Coinsurance Condition and the Agreed Value Optional Coverage, both present. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An applicability sentence only. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately describes the layered condition structure of the policy. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One flat sentence; 'abandonment' is a settled insurance term. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Loss Payment E.4.a.(3) allowing the insurer to take property at an agreed value. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Appraisal on the demand of 'either' party is mandatory in form; the OCR has eaten 'Pay its chosen appraiser', but the mechanism is standard. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 F. (Kansas Changes) replaces this condition with one under which appraisal happens 'only if both you and we agree, voluntarily' — a direct reversal of the demand right. Express replacement, but the two texts contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eight enumerated duties plus an examination-under-oath right; 'as soon as possible' and 'reasonably required' are soft but conventional. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties to Loss Payment's 30-day proof-of-loss trigger and to the Legal Action condition's 'full compliance with all of the terms'. Coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insurer's four-way option plus b.'s statement that repair cost 'does not include the increased cost attributable to enforcement of any ordinance or law' — that carve-out is a contestable boundary in a fire loss governed by building codes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely meets the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (A.4.e), whose e.(9) says the costs addressed in the Loss Payment Condition do not include ordinance-driven cost but that the ICC amount is not subject to that limitation. Reading the two together is genuinely awkward.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recovered-property mechanics stated plainly with an insured's option. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Abandonment and with Loss Payment. No conflict.
